title: B200: provisional SKU detection + hard compatibility gate (require explicit profile_version)
author: Yuki Sato
description: Context: We’re starting to see early B200 nodes in benchmark-lab and (soon) limited fleet. Today the runtime’s profile selection will happily fall back to “closest known” defaults (currently H100-ish) if it can’t match a SKU/driver/CUDA tuple, which is unsafe for bring-up and creates hard-to-debug perf/latency regressions due to kernel fallbacks + memory headroom differences. This PR adds provisional B200 SKU detection and introduces a hard compatibility gate: if the runtime detects B200 and the operator has not explicitly pinned a profile pack version, we refuse to start with defaults (Hosted/Dedicated) and emit a clear error. For Private, we fail closed by default, with an escape hatch for lab/dev only. Summary of behavior changes: (1) Detect B200 reliably via NVML PCI device ID + compute capability and surface sku=B200 in the runtime hardware fingerprint. (2) Add compatibility gate for B200: require runtime.profile_version (or env REDWOOD_PROFILE_VERSION) to be explicitly set and present in the loaded profile pack; otherwise exit with code 78 and message directing to docs/runbook. (3) Validate driver/CUDA baseline for B200 against allowlist in the profile pack metadata (min_driver, min_cuda). If out of range: refuse to start with actionable error that includes detected versions and supported range. (4) Add a “compatibility_reject_reason” structured log field and counter metric runtime_profile_compat_reject_total{sku,reason} to support SRE visibility during bring-up. (5) Wire the gate into both startup selection and per-model load (to avoid bypass when models are hot-reloaded across pools). Non-goals: This does not introduce a final B200 tuning profile; it only ensures we don’t accidentally run unknown defaults on B200 and that the selection path is deterministic and observable. Rollout notes: Hosted canary will use explicit profile_version in the canary config; Dedicated remains opt-in and customers can pin the version; Private installer will be updated in a separate PR to warn/fail earlier (tracked in ENG-4928). Testing: Added unit tests for detection parsing and selection gating; added an integration-ish test that mocks NVML fingerprint + config combinations; ran benchmark-lab smoke on one early B200 node with explicit profile_version=1.22.0-b200preview to confirm no spurious reject. Risk: Medium (changes startup behavior for a new SKU only). Existing H100/L40S behavior unchanged except for additional logging fields when hardware fingerprinting runs.
commits: runtime/hw: add provisional B200 detection via NVML device id + cc mapping
profiles: extend compatibility metadata schema (min_driver/min_cuda per sku) for gating
runtime/profiles: require explicit profile_version when sku==B200 (fail closed)
runtime/profiles: enforce driver/CUDA allowlist for B200 and include actionable error text
obs: add runtime_profile_compat_reject_total and structured reject_reason log field
tests: add selection gate tests + model reload regression coverage
implementation_notes: Detection: We map NVML device PCI IDs for early B200 samples to sku=B200 and validate with compute capability >= 10.0 when available (guarding against misreported PCI IDs on some virtualization layers). Selection/gating: selection.ts now checks detectedSku before applying any default profile resolution. If sku==B200 and profile_version is unset, we error early (before allocating GPU memory). Compatibility: compatibility.ts validates (a) profile pack supports sku, (b) detected driver/cuda meet the pack’s required minimums for that sku, and (c) profile_version exists in the pack index. Observability: we increment runtime_profile_compat_reject_total with a stable reason enum: missing_profile_version | profile_version_not_found | driver_too_old | cuda_too_old | sku_unsupported. Private escape hatch: REDWOOD_ALLOW_UNSAFE_DEFAULTS=1 will bypass missing_profile_version only, but still enforces sku support and min driver/cuda; the bypass is intentionally noisy (WARN log + metric runtime_profile_unsafe_bypass_total).
testing: Unit: selection_gate.test covers B200 + no pin => reject; B200 + bad pin => reject; B200 + valid pin + supported driver/cuda => ok; H100/L40S remain allowed without explicit pin. Unit: fingerprint_b200 validates NVML device id parsing and stable stringification in hardware fingerprint. Integration-ish: reload_profile_gate ensures a model reload path cannot bypass the gate (fix for earlier drift when models were moved across pools). Manual: ran on benchmark-lab b200-smoke node with pinned profile_version and validated /health includes sku=B200 and active profile_version.
rollout_plan: 1) Land behind existing profile pack feature flag (no behavior for non-B200). 2) Benchmark-lab: enable on B200 nodes with explicit profile_version in runner config; monitor runtime_profile_compat_reject_total. 3) Hosted: keep disabled globally; if any B200 enters fleet unexpectedly, this PR ensures we fail closed instead of silently using unsafe defaults. 4) Dedicated/Private: document requirement to pin profile_version for B200 bring-up; follow-up PRs will update installer/helm defaults to require the pin explicitly.
review_conversation: Noah Patel: I like failing closed, but please confirm we’re not going to brick existing H100 pools if fingerprinting misclassifies. Also, ensure the gate runs before any GPU allocations (we’ve had cases where OOM happens before config validation). Yuki Sato: Confirmed: the gate only triggers when detectedSku resolves to B200, and we require BOTH NVML PCI ID match and cc>=10 when cc is present. For safety we default to Unknown rather than B200 if signals conflict. Also moved the gate to run immediately after fingerprinting, before model load / allocator init; added a small test ensuring we don’t touch KV cache init when rejecting. Irene Choi: Driver baseline logic: please avoid hardcoding driver versions in code. Where does the allowlist live and how do we update it as infra standardizes? Yuki Sato: Agree—no hardcoded versions. The minimums live in the profile pack metadata (config/profile_pack.schema.json + pack index). Infra can bump the pack requirements when we standardize, and the runtime just enforces the pack contract. Quentin Harris: Versioning question: if profile_version is set but the pack doesn’t contain it, do we fall back? I strongly prefer no fallback for B200. Yuki Sato: No fallback. For B200 any mismatch is a hard error. For other SKUs, behavior unchanged (fallback allowed per existing rules). Sean Gallagher: Can we ensure the failure is visible to on-call? Need a metric and structured log fields for easy filtering. Also please use a distinct exit code so our supervisors can classify. Yuki Sato: Added runtime_profile_compat_reject_total{reason} + structured log with reject_reason + detected driver/cuda + sku. Exit code set to 78 (config error) so supervisor can distinguish from crash loops. Connor O’Brien: Please add changelog entry and a short note in internal docs so release notes don’t miss this. Yuki Sato: Added changelog/unreleased entry and a short section to docs/internal/runtime/profile-pack.md under “B200 bring-up requirements”. Noah Patel (follow-up): One more: ensure model hot-reload can’t bypass. We’ve seen selection rerun on reload with different context. Yuki Sato: Added reload_profile_gate test and forced selection to re-validate against the same pinned profile_version on reload; rejection is sticky (we don’t continue with a partially loaded model). Approvals: Noah Patel approved after changes; Irene Choi approved; Sean Gallagher approved with note to wire alerting in observability-pack; Connor O’Brien approved.
ci_checks: build-runtime (linux-x86_64): pass; unit-tests: pass; lint: pass; typecheck: pass; gpu-sim-tests: pass; perf-smoke (H100): skipped (not required); perf-smoke (B200): allowed-to-fail (not wired here). Initial run failed unit-tests due to brittle expected error string; fixed by asserting on reason enum + substring.
release_notes: Runtime will now fail closed on B200 unless an explicit profile pack version is pinned and compatible with the detected driver/CUDA; adds new compatibility reject metric for bring-up visibility.
